task.title: Tombstone-preserving replica merge
task.specification: config={} . Events {key:string,version:nonnegative integer,actor:ASCII string,deleted:boolean,value:ASCII string}. Retain the maximum event per key under the lexicographic tuple (version, deleted?1:0, actor, value). Deleted events must have value=''. Thus deletion wins a same-version write regardless of actor, and ties have a total public order. Output {visible,tombstones}: visible maps each live key to its value; tombstones is sorted deleted keys. An older write never resurrects a newer deletion; a higher-version write may replace it. Repeated and permuted deliveries must converge. Return one JSON output per event; state is opaque JSON, initially null. Objects in outputs have exactly the documented keys; map keys are unordered, arrays are ordered. Sorted/lexicographic string order compares Unicode scalar values (code points), with a shorter prefix first. Numeric inputs/values and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers. Integral JSON number notations such as 1 and 1.0 denote the same number, while booleans are distinct. Strings contain Unicode scalar values (no unpaired surrogates). Decoded imported values outside these limits are invalid frames. There are at most 48 events. Unknown/invalid operations have the behavior below. Each instance starts fresh. Hidden ordinary cases vary legal values; boundary cases emphasize equality, empty data and duplicates; adversarial cases reorder and conflict; shift cases use longer traces and more identities within the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Archival provenance and original order
matchedCard.relation: The origin and original arrangement of records preserve relationships that can be lost when the same contents are rearranged arbitrarily. A later description or arrangement is distinct from evidence of the organization in which the records were produced.
assumptions: The origin or original order is known or supported by evidence.
Relationships among records contribute to their interpretation.
matchedCard.boundary: Original order can be lost or disrupted. A newly devised arrangement does not establish that it was the historical arrangement, and provenance does not make every recorded claim true.
matchedCard.source_fact: The National Archives explains provenance, preserving or restoring original order, and devising arrangements when necessary, emphasizing the evidential significance of context.

shuffledCard.label: Seed banking
shuffledCard.relation: Preserving a reserve and preserving its ability to reactivate are different conditions. Suitable material remains in controlled storage, while periodic sample recovery provides evidence of continued viability. Duplicate holdings reduce dependence on one location.
assumptions: The material tolerates the chosen storage treatment.
Samples provide relevant evidence about the collection they represent.
Duplicate collections remain identifiable as corresponding holdings.
shuffledCard.boundary: Some material cannot survive drying or freezing. Successful retention alone does not demonstrate viability, and sampled viability is not certainty about every stored item.
shuffledCard.source_fact: Kew stores suitable dried seeds in cold vaults, periodically tests germination, and commonly duplicates holdings in their country of origin. Some seeds do not tolerate conventional storage.

sources.title: How to preserve seeds for the future

initial.explanation: Rule: for each key, retain the event with maximum (version, deleted, actor, value); expose it as visible unless deleted, otherwise list the key in sorted order. This preserves tombstones and makes delivery order irrelevant. A lower-version write cannot defeat a deletion; same-version deletion wins. The foil changes an emitted value or key, violating this invariant.
initial.mapping: Input events map to per-key maxima; maxima map to visible values or tombstone keys. State stores the current winning event for each key.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated event and JSON constraints. Sorting uses Unicode code-point order.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){function cp(a,b){var x=Array.from(a),y=Array.from(b),n=Math.min(x.length,y.length);for(var i=0;i<n;i++){var p=x[i].codePointAt(0),q=y[i].codePointAt(0);if(p!=q)return p-q}return x.length-y.length}function better(a,b){if(!b)return true;if(a.version!=b.version)return a.version>b.version;if(!!a.deleted!=!!b.deleted)return a.deleted?1:-1;var c=cp(a.actor,b.actor);if(c)return c>0;return cp(a.value,b.value)>0}var m={};for(var e of input.events)if(better(e,m[e.key]))m[e.key]=e;var v={},t=[];for(var k in m)if(m[k].deleted)t.push(k);else v[k]=m[k].value;t.sort(cp);if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!=input.events.length)return false;for(var i=0;i<output.length;i++){var mm={};for(var j=0;j<=i;j++)if(better(input.events[j],mm[input.events[j].key]))mm[input.events[j].key]=input.events[j];var vv={},tt=[];for(var z in mm)if(mm[z].deleted)tt.push(z);else vv[z]=mm[z].value;tt.sort(cp);if(JSON.stringify(output[i])!==JSON.stringify({visible:vv,tombstones:tt}))return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve(x){var s=x.state||{},m=s.m||{},e=x.event;function cp(a,b){var x=Array.from(a),y=Array.from(b),n=Math.min(x.length,y.length);for(var i=0;i<n;i++){var p=x[i].codePointAt(0),q=y[i].codePointAt(0);if(p!==q)return p-q}return x.length-y.length}function win(a,b){if(!b)return true;if(a.version!==b.version)return a.version>b.version;if(!!a.deleted!==!!b.deleted)return !!a.deleted;var c=cp(a.actor,b.actor);return c?c>0:cp(a.value,b.value)>0}if(win(e,m[e.key]))m[e.key]={key:e.key,version:e.version,actor:e.actor,deleted:e.deleted,value:e.value};var v={},t=[];for(var k in m){if(m[k].deleted)t.push(k);else v[k]=m[k].value}t.sort(cp);return {state:{m:m},output:{visible:v,tombstones:t}}}

final.explanation: For each key, retain the event with the greatest tuple (version, deletion flag, actor, value), comparing strings by Unicode code point. Recompute visible values and sorted tombstones after each delivery. Storing winning records makes duplicate and permuted deliveries converge, while tombstones prevent older writes from resurrecting deleted keys.

initial.explanation: For each key, retain the event with maximum (version, deletion flag, actor, value). Deletions are retained as tombstones and suppress older writes. Emit live values and sorted tombstone keys after every event.
initial.mapping: Each state record maps key to [version, deletedFlag, actor, value]. The output is derived from the retained records: nondeleted records populate visible; deleted records populate tombstones.
initial.assumptions: Inputs conform to the stated event schema and numeric/string limits. JavaScript code-point comparison is implemented explicitly rather than relying on UTF-16 ordering.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(const o of output){if(!o||Object.keys(o).length!==2||!o.visible||!Array.isArray(o.tombstones))return false;for(const k of o.tombstones)if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(o.visible,k)||k.includes('__changed'))return false;for(const k in o.visible)if(typeof o.visible[k]!=='string'||o.visible[k].includes('__changed'))return false;for(let i=1;i<o.tombstones.length;i++)if(cmp(o.tombstones[i-1],o.tombstones[i])>=0)return false}return true}function cmp(a,b){const x=Array.from(a),y=Array.from(b),n=Math.min(x.length,y.length);for(let i=0;i<n;i++)if(x[i]!==y[i])return x[i]<y[i]?-1:1;return x.length-y.length}
initial.program: function solve({config,state,event}){const s=state||{};const better=(a,b)=>{if(!b)return true;if(a[0]!==b[0])return a[0]>b[0];if(a[1]!==b[1])return a[1]>b[1];const c=(x,y)=>{const u=Array.from(x),v=Array.from(y),n=Math.min(u.length,v.length);for(let i=0;i<n;i++)if(u[i]!==v[i])return u[i]>v[i]?1:-1;return u.length-v.length};let z=c(a[2],b[2]);return z?z>0:c(a[3],b[3])>0};const r=[event.version,event.deleted?1:0,event.actor,event.value];if(better(r,s[event.key]))s[event.key]=r;const visible={},tombstones=[],keys=Object.keys(s);for(const k of keys){const q=s[k];if(q[1])tombstones.push(k);else visible[k]=q[3]}const cmp=(a,b)=>{const x=Array.from(a),y=Array.from(b),n=Math.min(x.length,y.length);for(let i=0;i<n;i++)if(x[i]!==y[i])return x[i]<y[i]?-1:1;return x.length-y.length};tombstones.sort(cmp);return {state:s,output:{visible,tombstones}}}

final.explanation: Retain one record per key, selecting the maximum tuple (version, deletion flag, actor, value) with explicit Unicode code-point comparison. The retained record determines whether a key is visible or a tombstone. Tombstone keys are sorted by code point order, and output maps safely preserve arbitrary string keys.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){const s=Array.isArray(state)?state:[],cp=(a,b)=>{const x=Array.from(a),y=Array.from(b),n=Math.min(x.length,y.length);for(let i=0;i<n;i++)if(x[i]!==y[i])return x[i]<y[i]?-1:1;return x.length-y.length},gt=(a,b)=>a[0]!==b[0]?a[0]>b[0]:a[1]!==b[1]?a[1]>b[1]:cp(a[2],b[2])?cp(a[2],b[2])>0:cp(a[3],b[3])>0,r=[event.version,event.deleted?1:0,event.actor,event.value];let i=-1;for(let j=0;j<s.length;j++)if(s[j][0]===event.key){i=j;break}if(i<0)s.push([event.key,r]);else if(gt(r,s[i][1]))s[i][1]=r;const visible={},tombstones=[];for(const e of s)if(e[1][1])tombstones.push(e[0]);else Object.defineProperty(visible,e[0],{value:e[1][3],enumerable:true,configurable:true,writable:true});tombstones.sort(cp);return{state:s,output:{visible:visible,tombstones:tombstones}}}

initial.explanation: For each key, retain the lexicographically greatest record by (version, deletion flag, actor, value). A deletion is therefore a durable tombstone until replaced by a strictly greater record. Reprocessing any record is harmless, and delivery order converges.
initial.mapping: The optional seed-bank analogy maps to retaining a recoverable reserve: records are retained, deletions preserve identity as tombstones, and duplicate deliveries correspond to duplicate holdings. The analogy does not override the specified tuple ordering or output format.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the published event and numeric limits. State is returned only to the same host and is not externally modified. JavaScript strings are compared by Unicode code points explicitly, rather than UTF-16 code units.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;let m={},cp=s=>Array.from(s),cmp=(a,b)=>{for(let i=0;i<4;i++){if(i===1){if(a[i]!==b[i])return a[i]-b[i]}else if(i===0){if(a[i]!==b[i])return a[i]-b[i]}else{let x=cp(a[i]),y=cp(b[i]),n=Math.min(x.length,y.length);for(let j=0;j<n;j++)if(x[j]!==y[j])return x[j]<y[j]?-1:1;if(x.length!==y.length)return x.length-y.length}}return 0};for(let i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){let e=input.events[i],r=[e.version,e.deleted?1:0,e.actor,e.value];if(!m[e.key]||cmp(r,m[e.key])>0)m[e.key]=r;let v={},t=[];for(let k in m)if(m[k][1])t.push(k);else v[k]=m[k][3];t.sort((a,b)=>{let x=cp(a),y=cp(b),n=Math.min(x.length,y.length);for(let j=0;j<n;j++)if(x[j]!==y[j])return x[j]<y[j]?-1:1;return x.length-y.length});if(JSON.stringify(output[i])!==JSON.stringify({visible:v,tombstones:t}))return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let r=state&&state.r?state.r:{};let e=event,k=e.key,n=[e.version,e.deleted?1:0,e.actor,e.value],a=r[k],cp=s=>Array.from(s),sc=(x,y)=>{let u=cp(x),v=cp(y),z=Math.min(u.length,v.length);for(let i=0;i<z;i++)if(u[i]!==v[i])return u[i]<v[i]?-1:1;return u.length-v.length},gt=(x,y)=>x[0]!==y[0]?x[0]>y[0]:x[1]!==y[1]?x[1]>y[1]:sc(x[2],y[2])||sc(x[3],y[3]);if(!a||gt(n,a))r[k]=n;let visible={},tombstones=[];for(let q in r)if(r[q][1])tombstones.push(q);else visible[q]=r[q][3];tombstones.sort(sc);return{state:{r:r},output:{visible:visible,tombstones:tombstones}}}

final.explanation: Each key stores its greatest delivered record under (version, deleted flag, actor, value), comparing strings by Unicode code points. Records are retained in an array, making duplicate and permuted delivery convergent and avoiding special-object-key hazards. Output is rebuilt after each event with live values and sorted tombstone keys.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let a=state&&Array.isArray(state.r)?state.r:[],e=event,i=a.findIndex(x=>x[0]===e.key),n=[e.key,e.version,e.deleted?1:0,e.actor,e.value],cp=s=>Array.from(s),cmp=(x,y)=>{let a=cp(x),b=cp(y),n=Math.min(a.length,b.length);for(let i=0;i<n;i++)if(a[i]!==b[i])return a[i]<b[i]?-1:1;return a.length-b.length},better=(x,y)=>x[1]!==y[1]?x[1]>y[1]:x[2]!==y[2]?x[2]>y[2]:cmp(x[3],y[3])>0||cmp(x[3],y[3])===0&&cmp(x[4],y[4])>0;if(i<0)a.push(n);else{let o=a[i];if(better(n,o))a[i]=n}let v={},t=[];for(let x of a)if(x[2])t.push(x[0]);else Object.defineProperty(v,x[0],{value:x[4],enumerable:true,writable:true,configurable:true});t.sort(cmp);return{state:{r:a},output:{visible:v,tombstones:t}}}
